references.title: Music organized by game usage
references.creator: Topfhelm
references.summary: A composer portfolio whose music is grouped by its role inside games instead of only by genre, release, or instrumentation.
references.takeaway: The listener immediately understands where each piece belongs: combat, exploration, character, atmosphere, interface, or narrative.
references.vois_application: Organize VOIS music by gameplay function, then show implementation context, adaptive behavior, and the scene or system each cue supports.

principles.title: Organize by the viewer's decision
principles.description: A recruiter should not need to decode the project. Group work by the question they are trying to answer: Can this person design combat audio? Can they build a game system? Can they communicate visual intent?

principles.title: Show evidence, not only output
principles.description: Pair the polished result with constraints, iteration, implementation details, and a concise explanation of what changed because of your work.

principles.title: One VOIS feature can serve several portfolios
principles.description: A timed-hit feature can become a game-design case study, a programming breakdown, a UI interaction piece, and a sound-design implementation example. Reuse evidence, not identical framing.

principles.title: Capture while the work is alive
principles.description: Record before-and-after images, short clips, diagrams, commits, failed approaches, and final decisions during development. Reconstructing them months later is expensive.

principles.title: Separate reference from imitation
principles.description: Store the exact pattern you admired, the underlying principle, and a distinct VOIS application. This turns inspiration into reusable knowledge instead of a mood board.

principles.title: Every case study needs a proof package
principles.description: Minimum evidence: final media, problem statement, your role, constraints, process, technical or design decisions, result, and one concrete lesson.
